## Add/Update Birthdate

Saves or updates a customer's **birthdate** in Flits. Use this endpoint to capture a customer's birthday so it can power **birthday rewards, loyalty campaigns, customer segmentation, marketing automation, and personalized experiences**. Calling it again for the same customer **updates** the stored birthdate.

> ⚠️ **Birthdate must be in `YYYY-MM-DD` format** (e.g., `2026-06-03`). Requests with any other format will be rejected.

---

### Authentication

This endpoint authenticates with the Flits token sent as a **form-data body field** (not a query parameter):

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | string | ✅ Yes | Your Flits API authentication token |

---

### Path Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `storeID` | string | ✅ Yes | Unique identifier of your Flits store |
| `customerID` | string | ✅ Yes | Unique identifier of the customer whose birthdate is being saved |

---

### Request Body

Sent as **`multipart/form-data`**.

| Field | Type | Required | Format | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `token` | string | ✅ Yes | — | Authentication token provided by Flits |
| `birthdate` | string | ✅ Yes | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Customer birthdate, e.g., `2026-06-03` |

---

### Birthdate Format

The `birthdate` value **must** follow the ISO-style `YYYY-MM-DD` pattern:

| Part | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `YYYY` | 4-digit year | `2026` |
| `MM` | 2-digit month (01–12) | `06` |
| `DD` | 2-digit day (01–31) | `03` |

✅ Valid: `2026-06-03`
❌ Invalid: `03-06-2026`, `2026/06/03`, `June 3 2026`, `2026-6-3`

In the **Try It** panel the `birthdate` field shows a `YYYY-MM-DD` placeholder and a format hint to help you supply a valid value.

---

### Example Request

``` bash
curl --location 'https://app.getflits.com/api/1/{{storeID}}/{{customerID}}/birthdate_save' \
--header 'accept: */*' \
--form 'token="{{flits_token}}"' \
--form 'birthdate="{{birthdate}}"'
```

---

## Code Samples

### cURL

``` bash
curl --location 'https://app.getflits.com/api/1/{{storeID}}/{{customerID}}/birthdate_save' \
--header 'accept: */*' \
--form 'token="{{flits_token}}"' \
--form 'birthdate="2026-06-03"'
```

### JavaScript (Node.js — fetch)

``` javascript
const storeID = process.env.STORE_ID;
const customerID = process.env.CUSTOMER_ID;
const token = process.env.FLITS_TOKEN;
const birthdate = '2026-06-03'; // YYYY-MM-DD

const form = new FormData();
form.append('token', token);
form.append('birthdate', birthdate);

const url = `https://app.getflits.com/api/1/${storeID}/${customerID}/birthdate_save`;
const response = await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'accept': '*/*' }, // do NOT set Content-Type — the boundary is added automatically
  body: form
});
const data = await response.json();
console.log(data);
```

### Python (requests)

``` python
import requests
import os
store_id = os.environ.get('STORE_ID')
customer_id = os.environ.get('CUSTOMER_ID')
token = os.environ.get('FLITS_TOKEN')
birthdate = '2026-06-03'  # YYYY-MM-DD

url = f"https://app.getflits.com/api/1/{store_id}/{customer_id}/birthdate_save"
# Using files=(None, value) forces a multipart/form-data request
files = {
    'token': (None, token),
    'birthdate': (None, birthdate),
}
response = requests.post(url, files=files, headers={'accept': '*/*'})
data = response.json()
print(data)
```

### PHP (cURL)

``` php
$storeID = getenv('STORE_ID');
$customerID = getenv('CUSTOMER_ID');
$token = getenv('FLITS_TOKEN');
$birthdate = '2026-06-03'; // YYYY-MM-DD

$url = "https://app.getflits.com/api/1/{$storeID}/{$customerID}/birthdate_save";
$ch = curl_init($url);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POST, true);
// Passing an array makes cURL send multipart/form-data
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, [
    'token' => $token,
    'birthdate' => $birthdate,
]);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, ['accept: */*']);
$response = curl_exec($ch);
curl_close($ch);
$data = json_decode($response, true);
print_r($data);
?>
```

### HTTP

``` http
POST /api/1/{{storeID}}/{{customerID}}/birthdate_save HTTP/1.1
Host: app.getflits.com
accept: */*
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----FlitsBoundary

------FlitsBoundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="token"

{{flits_token}}
------FlitsBoundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="birthdate"

2026-06-03
------FlitsBoundary--
```

---

### Example Response

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Birthdate saved successfully.",
  "data": {
    "birthdate": "2026-06-03"
  }
}
```

---

### Notes

- **Format is strict** — always send `birthdate` as `YYYY-MM-DD` (zero-padded month and day). Other formats return `400 Bad Request`.
- The request is **`multipart/form-data`** — do not set a `Content-Type: application/json` header. When using `fetch`/cURL/`requests` as shown, the multipart boundary is added automatically.
- This endpoint both **creates and updates** — sending a new `birthdate` for a customer overwrites the previous value.
- `token` is sent in the **body**, not the query string, for this endpoint.
- Once saved, the birthdate can drive birthday automations and segmentation in Flits.

## Customer Profile

The **Customer Profile** APIs allow merchants to retrieve and manage customer profile information stored in Flits. Use these endpoints to build customer account pages, enable profile editing, and collect birthdate information for birthday reward campaigns.

| API | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Get Profile** | Returns the complete profile for a customer — personal details (name, email, phone, gender, birthdate), loyalty points balance, store credit balance, VIP tier status, and other Flits-specific customer data. |
| **Update Profile** | Updates one or more customer profile fields. All fields are optional — send only the fields you want to change. Supported fields: `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone`, `birthdate`, `gender`. Changes are synced back to Shopify. |
| **Add/Update Birthdate** | Saves or updates a customer's birthdate (format: `YYYY-MM-DD`). Send an empty string to clear the birthdate. Used for birthday reward campaigns and personalized loyalty experiences. |

---

### Common use cases

- Build a customer account page with full profile information.
- Allow customers to edit their personal details directly from your storefront.
- Collect birthdates for birthday reward programs.
- Sync customer profile data between Flits and external systems.

---

### Validation notes

- **Phone number** — Must match the format expected by Shopify. Duplicate phone numbers across customers return a validation error.
- **First name** — Maximum 255 characters.
- **Birthdate** — Must use `YYYY-MM-DD` format. Invalid formats return a validation error.
- All profile fields are optional for `Update Profile` — partial updates are supported.

---

### Authentication

All endpoints require a Flits API token. The birthdate endpoint uses `multipart/form-data` with the token in the request body (not the query string).

```
?token={{flits_token}}   (Get Profile, Update Profile)
```

Requests are scoped to a store (`{{storeID}}`) and customer (`{{customerID}}`).

## Flits Loyalty

The **Flits Loyalty** by [Flits](https://getflits.com) enables Shopify merchants to integrate a fully-featured customer rewards system into their storefront. This collection covers all endpoints required to power loyalty points, store credits, referral programs, VIP tiers, and customer profile management on your customer account page.

---

### Overview

| Feature | Description |
| --- | --- |
| **Loyalty Points** | Reward customers for purchases, referrals, birthdays, and more |
| **Store Credits** | Issue and track store credit balances (e.g., from refunds or manual adjustments) |
| **Referral Program** | Let customers share referral links and earn points for successful referrals |
| **VIP Tiers** | Reward top customers with tiered status, exclusive benefits, and tier activity tracking |
| **Customer Profile** | Retrieve and manage customer profile information, including birthdate and contact details |
| **Balance Adjustment** | Manually add or deduct a customer's loyalty points or store credits, with a recorded reason |
| **Points Estimation** | Estimate the loyalty points a customer will earn for an order before it is placed |
| **Localization** | Fetch language-specific UI labels for all loyalty-related sections |

---

### Base URL

```
https://app.getflits.com/api/1

 ```

All requests use the `base_url` variable. Set this in your environment or collection variables.

---

### Authentication

All endpoints require a **Flits API token** passed as a query parameter:

```
?token={{flits_token}}

 ```

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `flits_token` | Your Flits API authentication token. This will be provided by Flits team |
| `storeID` | Your unique Flits store identifier. This will be provided by Flits team. |
| `customerID` | The ID of the customer making the request |
| `language_code` | Language code for localized content (e.g., `en`, `fr`, `de`) |

> Set these variables in the **Flits** environment before running any requests. 
  

---

### Collection Structure

| Folder | Key APIs | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Reward Program** | Get Earn & Redeem Rules, Get Customer Available Spent Rule, Get Customer Points Balance, Get Loyalty Points Activity, Apply Loyalty Points, Get Language Content | Loyalty points — earn & redeem rules, points balance, activity history, and redemption |
| **Referral** | Get Referral Data | Referral program details, referral codes, and earned rewards |
| **VIP Tier** | Get Current Tier, Get Customer Benefits, Get Tier Activity | VIP tier status, tier benefits, and tier activity history |
| **Store Credit** | Get Customer Store Credits Balance, Get Store Credits Activity, Get Customer Available Spent Rule, Apply Store Credit, Get Language Content | Store credit balance, activity history, and redemption |
| **Balance Adjustment** | Adjust Points or Credits | Manually add or deduct a customer's loyalty points or store credits |
| **Points Estimation** | Estimate Loyalty Points | Estimate the points a customer will earn for an order before it is placed |
| **Customer Profile** | Get Profile, Update Profile, Add/Update Birthdate | Customer profile management and birthdate tracking |

---

### Response Codes

All endpoints follow a consistent response structure:

| Status Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200 OK` | Request succeeded. Response body contains the requested data. |
| `400 Bad Request` | A required parameter is missing or has an invalid value. |
| `401 Unauthorized` | The `token` is missing, expired, or invalid. |
| `404 Not Found` | The specified `storeID` or `customerID` does not exist. |
| `500 Internal Server Error` | An unexpected server-side error occurred. |

---

### Quick Setup

1. Open the **Flits** environment.
    
2. Set the following variables:
    
    - `base_url` → `https://app.getflits.com/api/1`
        
    - `storeID` → your Flits store ID
        
    - `customerID` → the customer's ID
        
    - `flits_token` → your Flits API token
        
    - `language_code` → e.g., `en`
        
3. Select the environment and run any request in the collection.
    

---

### Resources

- [Flits Website](https://getflits.com)
    

---

### Rate Limiting

> **Current Status:** No hard rate limits are enforced on this API at this time. 
  

While there are no enforced rate limits currently, we recommend following these best practices to ensure stable integrations:

| Recommendation | Details |
| --- | --- |
| **Avoid burst requests** | Do not fire multiple requests simultaneously for the same customer in rapid succession |
| **Cache responses** | Cache balance and rules responses client-side for 30–60 seconds to reduce redundant calls |
| **Paginate activity feeds** | Use the `page` parameter when fetching activity history instead of loading all records at once |
| **Retry with backoff** | If you receive a `500` response, wait at least 1–2 seconds before retrying |

> ⚠️ Rate limits may be introduced in future API versions. Monitor the [Flits changelog](https://getflits.com) for updates. 
  

---

### Standard Error Response Format

All error responses follow a consistent JSON structure:

```json
{
  "status": false,
  "error": "A human-readable description of what went wrong"
}
```

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | boolean | `false` for all error responses |
| `error` | string | Human-readable error message |

---

### HTTP Status Code Reference

| Code | Name | When It Occurs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | OK | Request succeeded. Response body contains the requested data |
| `400` | Bad Request | Missing or invalid request parameters (e.g., missing `language_code`, invalid `token` format) |
| `401` | Unauthorized | The `token` query parameter is missing, expired, or does not match the store |
| `404` | Not Found | The `storeID` or `customerID` does not exist in the Flits system |
| `500` | Internal Server Error | An unexpected server-side error occurred. Retry after a short delay |

---

### Troubleshooting Guide

#### ❌ `401 Unauthorized` — Token Issues

**Symptoms:** All requests return `401` regardless of endpoint.

**Checklist:**

1. Verify `flits_token` is set in your active environment (`Flits`)
    
2. Confirm the token belongs to the correct store — tokens are store-scoped
    
3. Check that the token has not expired or been rotated in your Flits dashboard
    
4. Ensure the token is passed as `?token=` in the query string, not as a header
    

---

#### ❌ `404 Not Found` — Store or Customer Not Found

**Symptoms:** Requests to customer-specific endpoints return `404`.

**Checklist:**

1. Verify `storeID` matches your Flits store identifier exactly (case-sensitive)
    
2. Confirm `customerID` is a valid Shopify customer ID associated with your store
    
3. Ensure the customer has an active account in Flits (new customers may not be synced yet)
    
4. For `Get Language Content`, confirm the store has the Flits Loyalty app installed and active
    

---

#### ❌ `400 Bad Request` — Missing or Invalid Parameters

**Symptoms:** Specific endpoints return `400` with validation errors.

**Checklist:**

1. For `Get Language Content`: ensure `language_code` is a valid ISO 639-1 code (e.g., `en`, `fr`, `de`)
    
2. For `Get Earn & Redeem Rules`: ensure `version=loyalty_update` is included in the query string
    
3. For activity endpoints: ensure `page` is a positive integer if provided
    
4. Check that no required environment variables are empty — open `Flits` environment and verify all five variables are populated
    

---

#### ❌ `500 Internal Server Error` — Server-Side Failures

**Symptoms:** Intermittent failures on otherwise valid requests.

**Recommended Actions:**

1. Wait 2–5 seconds and retry the request
    
2. Check if the issue is isolated to one endpoint or affects all endpoints
    
3. If the issue persists for more than 5 minutes, contact [Flits Support](https://getflits.com)
    
4. Include the full request URL (with parameters redacted) and timestamp when reporting
    

---

#### ❌ "Could Not Load Examples" in Documentation

**Symptoms:** Published documentation shows "Could Not Load Examples" for some requests.

**Resolution:** All requests in this collection now have saved examples (200 OK, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error). If you still see this error, try refreshing the documentation page or re-publishing the collection.

---

### Environment Setup Checklist

Before making any requests, ensure all variables are set in the **Flits** environment:

| Variable | Example Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `base_url` | `https://app.getflits.com/api/1` | Base URL for all API requests |
| `storeID` | `your-store-id` | Your unique Flits store identifier |
| `customerID` | `shopify-customer-id` | The Shopify customer ID to query |
| `flits_token` | `your-api-token` | Your Flits API authentication token |
| `language_code` | `en` | ISO 639-1 language code for localized content |

## Add to Wishlist

Adds one or more products to a customer's wishlist. Supports both logged-in and guest customers.

### Guest vs. Logged-in Support

| Customer Type | Supported | How to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Logged-in customer** | ✅ Yes | Set `is_guest: false` and provide `customer_email`. The `shopify_customer_id` is not required in the body but must be available for downstream operations. |
| **Guest customer** | ⚠️ Partial | Set `is_guest: true` and omit `customer_email`. Guest wishlist items are stored against a `guest_customer_id`. Use the **Link Guest to Shopify Customer** endpoint after login to migrate guest items to the customer's account. |

> **Note:** This request currently defaults to `is_guest: false` (logged-in user). To test guest behaviour, change `is_guest` to `true` and remove the `customer_email` field. 
  

---

### Add to Wishlist

This endpoint adds one or more products to a shopper's wishlist. It is used for **logged-in users** (`is_guest: false`) and requires `operation: "create"` and `action: "wishlisted"`.

---

### HTTP Request

- **Method:** `POST`
    
- **URL:** `https://wishlist.getflits.com/core/wishlist/actions`
    

---

### Headers

| Header | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Request body is JSON. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `merchant_id` | `{{merchant_id}}` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |

---

### Request Body

The request body is a **raw JSON array** containing one or more wishlist action objects.

> **Note:** `operation` must always be `"create"` and `action` must always be `"wishlisted"` for this endpoint. 
  

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant_id` | `string` | Required | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `operation` | `string` | Required | Must be `"create"` for adding items. |
| `action` | `string` | Required | Must be `"wishlisted"`. |
| `is_guest` | `boolean` | Required | `false` for logged-in users; `true` for guests. |
| `customer_email` | `string` | Required | Email address of the logged-in customer. |
| `product_id` | `number` | Required | Shopify product ID. |
| `variant_id` | `number` | Required | Shopify variant ID. |
| `product_handle` | `string` | Required | URL handle/slug of the product. |
| `product_title` | `string` | Required | Display title of the product. |

### Remove from Wishlist

Removes one or more products from a shopper's wishlist. Supports both **logged-in users** and **guest users** by specifying the appropriate `shopify_customer_id` or `guest_id` in the filters.

---

### HTTP Request

- **Method:** `POST`
    
- **URL:** `https://wishlist.getflits.com/core/wishlist/actions`
    

---

### Headers

| Header | Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Request payload format. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `merchant_id` | `{{merchant_id}}` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |

---

### Request Body

The body is a JSON **array** of action objects. Each object represents a single remove operation.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant_id` | `string` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `operation` | `string` | Yes | Must be `"delete"` to remove an item. |
| `filters` | `object` | Yes | Identifies the customer and item to remove. |
| `filters.shopify_customer_id` | `string` | Yes\* | Shopify customer ID (for logged-in users). |
| `product_id` | `number` | Yes | Shopify product ID of the item to remove. |
| `variant_id` | `number` | Yes | Shopify variant ID of the item to remove. |

> \*Use `shopify_customer_id` for logged-in users. For guest users, use the appropriate guest identifier in the `filters` object.

| `200 OK` | Item successfully removed from the wishlist. |
| `400 Bad Request` | Invalid request payload or operation value. |
| `404 Not Found` | The specified item was not found in the wishlist. |

---

### Notes

- The `operation` field must be `"delete"` for removal actions.
    
- Both `product_id` and `variant_id` must be provided to uniquely identify the wishlist item.
    
- Multiple items can be removed in a single request by adding more objects to the array.

## Get Wishlist Data

Queries a customer's wishlist items with filter and pagination support. Returns all wishlisted products matching the specified criteria.

### Guest vs. Logged-in Support

| Customer Type | Supported | How to use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Logged-in customer** | ✅ Yes | Pass the customer's `shopify_customer_id` in the `filters.shopify_customer_id` field. |
| **Guest customer** | ⚠️ Limited | Guest wishlist data is not directly queryable via this endpoint using a `shopify_customer_id`. To retrieve guest wishlist items, use the guest session identifier if supported, or link the guest to a Shopify customer first using the **Link Guest to Shopify Customer** endpoint. |

> **Note:** This endpoint is primarily designed for logged-in customer queries. Guest wishlist retrieval may require a separate flow. 
  

---

## Get Wishlist Data

Queries wishlist items for a specific merchant and customer. This endpoint accepts filter and pagination/sorting options, and returns a list of wishlisted products matching the given criteria. It is primarily used to retrieve the current state of a customer's wishlist from third-party integrations.

---

## Authentication

This endpoint requires two forms of identification:

- **Bearer JWT Token** — This will be provided by Flits Team.
    
- **Merchant ID Header** — This will be provided by Flits Team.
    

Both must be present for the request to be authorized.

---

## Request Headers

| Header | Value | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Yes | Indicates the request body is JSON. |
| `merchant_id` | `{{merchant_id}}` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |

---

## Request Body

The request body must be a JSON object with the following top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant_id` | `string` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `filters` | `object` | Yes | Criteria used to filter the wishlist items returned. See **Filters** below. |
| `options` | `object` | Yes | Controls pagination, caching, and sorting behavior. See **Options** below. |

### Filters Object

The `filters` object narrows down which wishlist items are returned.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shopify_customer_id` | `string` | Yes | The Shopify customer ID whose wishlist items should be fetched. |
| `deleted_at` | `string` | Optional | If provided, filters items based on their deletion timestamp. Pass `null` to fetch active items. |

### Options Object

The `options` object controls how results are fetched and ordered.

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `integer` | Yes | Maximum number of wishlist items to return. Default in this request is `10000`. |
| `use_cache` | `boolean` | Yes | Whether to use cached results. Set to `false` to always fetch fresh data from the source. |
| `sort_field` | `string` | Yes | The field to sort results by. Example: `"updated_at"`. |
| `sort_direction` | `string` | Yes | Sort order — `"ASC"` for ascending or `"DESC"` for descending. Default in this request is `"DESC"`. |

---

## Example Request Body

``` json
{
  "merchant_id": "{{merchant_id}}",
  "filters": {
    "shopify_customer_id": "{{shopify_customer_id}}",
    "deleted_at": "{{deleted_at}}"
  },
  "options": {
    "limit": 10000,
    "use_cache": false,
    "sort_field": "updated_at",
    "sort_direction": "DESC"
  }
}

 ```

---

## Responses

This endpoint has two documented success scenarios:

**`200 - Success`**  
Returned when the customer has one or more wishlist items. The response body contains the list of wishlisted products matching the applied filters and options.

**`200 - Success (Empty Wishlist)`**  
Returned when the customer exists but has no wishlist items. The response body will reflect an empty result set rather than an error.

---

## Notes

- **Caching** — Setting `use_cache: false` ensures the response reflects the latest data. Enable caching (`true`) in read-heavy scenarios where real-time accuracy is not critical.
    
- **Sorting** — Results are sorted by `updated_at` in descending order by default, meaning the most recently updated wishlist items appear first.
    
- **Limit** — The default limit is set to `10000`. Adjust this value based on expected wishlist size to avoid over-fetching.
    
- **Variables** — This request uses the following Postman variables: `BASE_URL`, `merchant_id`, `shopify_customer_id`, and `deleted_at`.

## Link Guest to Shopify Customer

Links a **guest customer** to an existing **Shopify customer account**. This is typically called after a guest user logs in or registers, to migrate their guest session (e.g., wishlist items) to their authenticated Shopify account.

---

### HTTP Request

- **Method:** `POST`
    
- **URL:** `https://wishlist.getflits.com/core/customers/link`
    

---

### Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` |
| `merchant_id` | `{{merchant_id}}` |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |

---

### Request Body

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `customer_id` | string | Yes | The internal Flits guest customer ID to be linked. |
| `shopify_customer_id` | string | Yes | The Shopify customer ID to link the guest account to. |
| `email` | string | Yes | The email address of the Shopify customer. |

**Example:**

``` json
{
  "customer_id": "{{guest_customer_id}}",
  "shopify_customer_id": "{{shopify_customer_id}}",
  "email": "{{email}}"
}

 ```

---

### Responses

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `200 OK` | Guest customer successfully linked to the Shopify customer. |
| `409 Conflict` | The guest customer is already linked to a Shopify customer account. |

---

### Notes

- Use the `guest_customer_id` variable to pass the guest's internal ID obtained before login.

## Wishlist Core

The **Wishlist Core** group contains the primary endpoints for managing a customer's wishlist. These APIs allow third-party integrations to add items to a wishlist, remove items, query the full wishlist, and link guest sessions to authenticated Shopify customers.

All endpoints in this group require a valid **JWT Bearer Token** and a **Merchant ID**. This will be provided by Flits Team.

---

### Endpoints in this Group

| Endpoint | Method | URL | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Add to Wishlist** | `POST` | `{{wishlist_base_url}}/core/wishlist/actions` | Add a product variant to a customer's wishlist. |
| **Remove from Wishlist** | `POST` | `{{wishlist_base_url}}/core/wishlist/actions` | Remove a specific product variant from a customer's wishlist. |
| **Get Wishlist Data** | `POST` | `{{wishlist_base_url}}/core/wishlist/items/query` | Query and retrieve all wishlist items for a customer, with filtering, sorting, and pagination support. |
| **Link Guest to Shopify Customer** | `POST` | `{{wishlist_base_url}}/core/customers/link` | Merge a guest session's wishlist into an authenticated Shopify customer account. |

---

### Get Wishlist Data

The **Get Wishlist Data** endpoint (`POST /core/wishlist/items/query`) is used to retrieve the current state of a customer's wishlist from third-party integrations. It supports flexible filtering, sorting, and result-limiting options.

#### Authentication

| Header | Value | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Yes | Request body format. |
| `merchant_id` | `{{merchant_id}}` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |

#### Request Body Parameters

**Top-level fields:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant_id` | `string` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `filters` | `object` | Yes | Criteria to filter which wishlist items are returned. |
| `options` | `object` | Yes | Controls pagination, caching, and sorting behaviour. |

**`filters`** **object:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shopify_customer_id` | `string` | Yes | The Shopify customer ID whose wishlist items should be fetched. |
| `deleted_at` | \`string | null\` | Optional |

**`options`** **object:**

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `integer` | Yes | Maximum number of items to return. Recommended default: `10000`. |
| `use_cache` | `boolean` | Yes | Set to `false` to always fetch fresh data. Set to `true` in read-heavy scenarios where real-time accuracy is not critical. |
| `sort_field` | `string` | Yes | Field to sort results by. Supported value: `"updated_at"`. |
| `sort_direction` | `string` | Yes | Sort order — `"ASC"` (oldest first) or `"DESC"` (newest first). |

#### Example Request Body

``` json
{
  "merchant_id": "{{merchant_id}}",
  "filters": {
    "shopify_customer_id": "{{shopify_customer_id}}",
    "deleted_at": null
  },
  "options": {
    "limit": 10000,
    "use_cache": false,
    "sort_field": "updated_at",
    "sort_direction": "DESC"
  }
}

 ```

#### Response Scenarios

| Status | Scenario | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | Success | Customer has one or more wishlist items. Returns the full list matching the applied filters. |
| `200` | Success (Empty Wishlist) | Customer exists but has no wishlist items. Returns an empty result set — not an error. |
| `400` | Bad Request — Missing `shopify_customer_id` | The `filters.shopify_customer_id` field was not provided in the request body. |
| `400` | Bad Request — Missing `merchant_id` | The `merchant_id` field was not provided in the request body. |
| `401` | Unauthorized | The `Authorization` header is missing or the JWT token is invalid/expired. |

#### Notes

- Setting `use_cache: false` ensures the response reflects the latest data. Enable caching in read-heavy scenarios where real-time accuracy is not critical.
    
- Results are sorted by `updated_at` in descending order by default — the most recently updated items appear first.
    
- The default `limit` is `10000`. Adjust based on expected wishlist size to avoid over-fetching.
    
- This request uses the Postman variables: `{{merchant_id}}`, `{{shopify_customer_id}}`, `{{deleted_at}}`, and `{{jwt_token}}`.
    

---

This folder contains requests for sending **customer behavior analytics events** to the [Flits analytics pipeline](https://analytics.getflits.com/) via the `save_analytics_event` action. All requests are `POST` requests to `https://analytics.getflits.com/` and require **Bearer token** authentication via the `Authorization` header.

Use these requests to track key storefront interactions — such as wishlist engagement and cart activity — for logged-in Shopify customers.

---

### Key points:

- **jwt_token** : This will be provided by Flits Team.
    
- **merchant_id** : This will be provided by Flits Team.
    

## Authentication

All requests in this folder use the same authentication scheme:

| Type | Header | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bearer Token | `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` |

> Make sure `jwt_token` is set in **Environment Variables** before sending any request. 
  

---

## Requests

### 1\. Wishlist Button Click

Tracks when a customer **clicks the wishlist button** on a product on a Shopify storefront.

- **Action:** `save_analytics_event`
    
- **Firehose Type:** `wishlist`
    
- **Event Name:** `wishlistClick`
    

#### Request Body Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `action` | string | Yes | Must be `"save_analytics_event"` |
| `merchant_id` | string | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `auth_token` | string | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `firehose_type` | string | Yes | Must be `"wishlist"` |
| `customer_id` | number | Yes | Shopify customer ID (`{{shopify_customer_id}}`) |
| `event_data` | array | Yes | Array containing a single event object |

#### `event_data[].data` Fields

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `event_name` | string | Yes | Must be `"wishlistClick"` |
| `dimensions.product_id` | number | Yes | Shopify product ID (`{{product_id}}`) |
| `dimensions.variant_id` | number | Yes | Shopify variant ID (`{{variant_id}}`) |

| `dimensions.customer_id` | number | Yes | Shopify customer ID (`{{shopify_customer_id}}`) |

---

### 2\. Add to Cart

Tracks when a customer **adds a product or variant to their cart** on a Shopify storefront.

- **Action:** `save_analytics_event`
    
- **Firehose Type:** `wishlist`

## Wishlist Share and Manage Collections

These storefront endpoints extend the Wishlist App with named **collections**, wishlist **sharing**, and advanced collection-scoped **item queries**.

- **Add/Remove Wishlist Items** — add/remove via `POST /core/wishlist/actions` (array body; supports `added_from_page` source tracking, back-in-stock contacts, and a `collections` array).

- **Shared Page** — read-only endpoints a share link's visitor calls.
- **Wishlist Items of Specific Collections** — keyset-paginated item query/search via `/core/wishlist/items/query` and `/core/wishlist/items/search` (filters, sorting, cursor pagination).

- **Owner / customer requests** use `Authorization: Bearer {{jwt_token}}` plus the `merchant_id: {{merchant_id}}` header — the same pattern as the rest of the Wishlist App.
- **Shared-page (visitor) requests** authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer share_{{share_token}}` — a read-only share token, no login required. Set `{{share_token}}` to the token returned by a share-creation request.

item.name: Wishlist Items of Specific Collections
item.description:
## Wishlist Items of Specific Collections

Query and search endpoints for reading wishlist items at scale — across the whole wishlist or scoped to a single collection. Every read uses one uniform request and response shape with filtering, sorting, and cursor-based (keyset) pagination, so results stay complete no matter how large the wishlist grows. The requests in this folder are worked examples, each demonstrating one capability — basic paging, filters, search, sorting, combined queries, and edge cases.

### Response shape

All endpoints return:

`{ "data": [ ... ], "pagination": { "limit", "count", "next_cursor", "total_count" } }`

### Pagination & count

Send the first page with no `options.cursor`; the response includes `total_count` and a `next_cursor`. For each following page, resend the same `filters` and sort and pass the previous `next_cursor` as `options.cursor` (echo `total_count` back via `options.total_count` so the server can skip re-counting). `next_cursor` is `null` on the last page.

### Vocabulary

- **filters:** `shopify_customer_id`, `customer_id`, `variant_id`, `product_id`, `collection_id`, `action`, plus `<key> in` variants.
- **filter_types / filter_types_or:** `wishlisted`, `back_in_stock`, `out_of_stock`, `price_drop`, `low_stock`.
- **search keys:** `all`, `product_title`, `product_handle`, `variant_title`, `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `shopify_customer_id`.
- **sort_field:** `created_at` (default), `updated_at`, `product_title`, `product_price`, `product_event_triggered_at`; **sort_direction:** `asc` or `desc`. **limit:** default 50, maximum 200.

### Requests in this folder

Each request is a worked example of one capability:

- **Pagination Walkthrough** — a two-request run showing cursor pagination end to end.
- **First Page (No Filters)** and **Next Page (Echo Cursor + Total Count)** — basic paging.
- **Filter from Shopify Customer ID**, **Filter from Variant IDs**, **Collection Scoped (Filter from Collection ID)**, **Filter from Back in Stock** and **Filter from Price Drop or Low Stock (OR)** — filtering.
- **Search from All Trail** and **Search by Customer Email** — keyword and customer search.
- **Sort by Product Price** and **Sort by Updated Product Event Triggered** — sorting.
- **Combined (Collection ID + Filter Type + Sort + Cursor)** and **Search with Notification Enabled and Event** — combined queries.
- **Empty Result**, **Error: Limit Over Cap (clamped, not rejected)** and **Error: Malformed Cursor** — edge cases.

## Pagination Walkthrough

A two-request example that shows how to page through wishlist items from start to finish using keyset (cursor-based) pagination.

1. Send **First Page (Page 1)** with no cursor. The response returns `pagination.total_count` (the grand total) and `pagination.next_cursor`.
2. Send **Next Page (Page 2+)** repeatedly, each time passing the previous response's `next_cursor` as `options.cursor` and echoing `total_count` back — keep the same `filters` and sort throughout.
3. Stop when `next_cursor` comes back `null`; that was the last page.

Do not change the filters or sort mid-run — a cursor is only valid for the query that produced it. In Try It, the returned `next_cursor` and `total_count` are captured into the `{{next_cursor}}` and `{{known_total}}` variables so the next request can reuse them.

exec: console.log('Saved next_cursor. total_count=' + p.total_count + '. Now run "Page 2+".');

item.description:
## Flits Wishlist

This collection provides everything a third-party developer needs to integrate with the **Flits Wishlist** for Shopify merchants. It covers customer wishlist management, analytics event tracking, and guest-to-customer session linking.

**Base URL — Wishlist Core:** `https://wishlist.getflits.com`  
**Base URL — Analytics Events:** `https://analytics.getflits.com`

---

## Getting Started

Follow these four steps to make your first successful API call.

### Step 1 — Obtain Your Credentials

Contact the **Flits team** to receive:

| Credential | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `jwt_token` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `merchant_id` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |

Keep these values secure. Do not expose them in client-side code or public repositories.

---

### Step 2 — Set Up Your Environment

This documentation uses environment variables so you never have to hard-code credentials. Set the following variables in the **Environment Variables** panel:

| Variable | Example Value | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `wishlist_base_url` | `https://wishlist.getflits.com` | Base URL for Wishlist Core endpoints. |
| `analytics_base_url` | `https://analytics.getflits.com` | Base URL for Analytics Events endpoints. |
| `jwt_token` | `eyJhbGci...` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `merchant_id` | `12345` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `shopify_customer_id` | `6789012345` | The Shopify customer ID you are operating on. |

Every request in this collection references these variables using the `{{variable_name}}` syntax — update them once and all requests stay in sync.

---

### Step 3 — Make Your First API Call

The simplest way to verify your setup is to call **Add to Wishlist**.

**Request:**

```
POST {{wishlist_base_url}}/core/wishlist/actions

 ```

**Headers:**

```
Content-Type:  application/json
Authorization: Bearer {{jwt_token}}
merchant_id:   {{merchant_id}}

 ```

**Body:**

``` antlr4
[
  {
    "merchant_id": "{{merchant_id}}",
    "operation": "create",

 ```

Open the **Add to Wishlist** request in the **Wishlist Core** folder, ensure your environment is selected, and click **Send**.

---

### Step 4 — Verify the Response

A successful response returns HTTP `201` with a JSON body confirming the item was added:

``` json
{
  "status": true,
  "message": "Item added to wishlist successfully.",
  "data": { ... }
}

 ```

If you receive a `401 Unauthorized`, double-check that your `jwt_token` and `merchant_id` environment variables are set correctly and that the token has not expired.

## Authentication & Configuration

All endpoints in this collection require the following headers on every request:

| Header | Value | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Content-Type` | `application/json` | Yes | All request bodies must be JSON. |
| `Authorization` | `Bearer {{jwt_token}}` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `merchant_id` | `{{merchant_id}}` | Yes | This will be provided by Flits Team. |

> **Note:** `{{jwt_token}}` and `{{merchant_id}}` above are environment variable placeholders. Replace them with your actual credentials when making requests. 
  
> These three headers are required on **every** request. Configure them once in **Environment Variables** and they are applied automatically across all requests.

## Data Model Glossary

The following identifiers appear across multiple endpoints. Understanding the distinction between them is critical for correct integration.

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `merchant_id` | string | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `shopify_customer_id` | string / number | The native Shopify customer ID (numeric). Identifies a logged-in, registered customer. Obtained from Shopify's customer object after authentication. |
| `customer_id` | string | The internal Flits customer ID. Used in analytics event bodies and some response payloads. Not the same as `shopify_customer_id`. |
| `guest_customer_id` | string | A temporary identifier assigned to a guest (unauthenticated) user session by the Flits platform. Used in the Link Guest endpoint to migrate a guest session to a Shopify customer account. |
| `guest_browser_id` | string | A browser fingerprint or device identifier used to track guest sessions across page loads. Appears in response payloads only — not required in request bodies. |
| `product_id` | number | The Shopify product ID. Identifies the parent product in the Shopify product hierarchy. |
| `variant_id` | number | The Shopify product variant ID. Identifies a specific variant (e.g., size, colour) of a product. Both `product_id` and `variant_id` are required together to uniquely identify a wishlist item. |

## Rate Limiting & Error Handling

### Rate Limits

There are currently **no enforced rate limits** on this API. However, we recommend:

- Avoiding tight polling loops — use event-driven calls instead.
    
- Batching requests where possible to reduce unnecessary load.
    

Rate limiting may be introduced in future versions. Check the changelog below for updates.

### CORS, TLS & Payload Policy

| Policy | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **TLS** | TLS 1.2 or higher is required for all connections. Requests over plain HTTP will be rejected. |
| **CORS** | CORS preflight (`OPTIONS`) requests are **not supported**. These APIs are designed for server-to-server integration only. Do not call them directly from browser-side JavaScript. |
| **Max request body size** | There is no documented hard limit, but we recommend keeping individual request payloads under **1 MB**. For bulk wishlist operations, batch items into multiple requests if needed. |

### Standard Error Response Format

All error responses follow a consistent JSON structure:

``` json
{
  "status": false,
  "message": "A human-readable description of the error.",
  "errors": { }
}

 ```

### HTTP Status Code Reference

| Status Code | Meaning | Common Cause |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `200` | OK | Request succeeded (used by query and analytics endpoints). |
| `201` | Created | Resource successfully created (used by Add/Remove Wishlist). |
| `400` | Bad Request | Missing or invalid request parameters. Check the `message` field. |
| `401` | Unauthorized | Missing, invalid, or expired JWT token. |
| `404` | Not Found | The requested resource does not exist (e.g., customer not found). |
| `409` | Conflict | Duplicate operation (e.g., guest already linked to a Shopify customer). |

### Support & Debugging

When filing a support ticket with the Flits team, include the following in your report to enable fast diagnosis:

| Field | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| `merchant_id` | This will be provided by Flits Team. |
| `shopify_customer_id` | The customer ID used in the failing request body or filter. |
| Timestamp (UTC) | The exact time the request was made. |
| Request endpoint | The full URL and HTTP method. |
| Response body | The full JSON error response returned by the API. |
| HTTP status code | The status code returned (e.g., `401`, `400`). |

> If the API returns an `x-request-id` response header, always include its value in your support ticket — it allows the Flits team to locate the exact server-side log entry for your request. 
  

### Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `401 Unauthorized` | Token missing or expired | Verify `{{jwt_token}}` is set in your environment and has not expired. Contact Flits team to re-issue if needed. |
| `400 Bad Request` | Missing required field | Read the `message` field in the response — it identifies the missing parameter. |
| `404 Not Found` | Invalid customer ID | Confirm `{{shopify_customer_id}}` is a valid Shopify customer ID for this merchant. |
| `409 Conflict` | Already linked | The guest session has already been linked to this Shopify customer. |
| Empty wishlist response | No items added yet | This is expected — a `200` with an empty result set is not an error. |

> **Note:** `{{jwt_token}}` and `{{shopify_customer_id}}` in the table above are environment variable placeholders — replace them with your actual values.
